Dear professionals, welcome to the new edition of our PFI newsletter. This issue includes an interview with Petr Knap, Senior Advisor, Mentor and Investor and explores key themes shaping global macro, equity valuation, corporate and investor-relations practice, Czech M&A, private equity, the banking sector and behavioral finance. In this issue of PFI Monthly you will find: Global macro – Headline versus core inflation: why central banks target the headline number households feel, yet read core, services and wage data to judge where inflation is actually heading. Financial markets – A cluster on valuation discipline: how to recognise value traps, why normalized (not peak) earnings belong in a P/E, how one megacap's non-operating gain can distort an entire earnings season, the AI narrative colliding with rising yields and geopolitical risk, and the case that the value premium comes from stocks that migrate, not from those that stay cheap. Corporate finance – The cash flow waterfall, and why tracing revenue all the way down to what remains for shareholders is one of the most effective tools in equity and credit analysis. Investor relations – "Silence is a financing decision": how illiquidity and low visibility quietly add to the cost of equity, and why that is a choice boards make by default. Czech M&A – Shimadzu's $711m acquisition of Brno-founded Tescan from Carlyle, the largest deal in the Japanese group's history. Private equity – Why FIFA's $20bn commercial rights transaction collapsed four days after launch, and what it reveals about ownership versus cash flows in sport. Banking sector – Systemic risk indicators near all-time lows while bank valuations soar: a study in compressed risk premia and fragile complacency. Behavioral finance – Framing bias: how the same information, presented differently, drives different decisions. Book review – The Fractalist: Memoir of a Scientific Maverick by Benoit Mandelbrot. 👉 Read the full edition to explore all insights in detail. We would also like to warmly thank partners of the Prague Finance Institute: CERGE-EI, Deník e15, KPMG Czech Republic, Conseq Investment Management, a.s., Oriens, PPF Group, TARPAN Partners, BHM group, RSJ Investments, ARETE, X Production s.r.o., White & Case LLP, Cushman & Wakefield, House of Julius Meinl Limited, Datasite and EKP Advisory. Sign up for free here to receive this newsletter in your inbox every Saturday. You’ll also get our weekly newsletter with an exclusive introduction from our editor-in-chief. What did you do on Friday night? If you woke up the next morning with a clear head, I expect you’re one of those priggish, strait-laced Gen Zs. If, on the other hand, you suffered from a creeping hangover and perhaps found an unfamiliar person in your bed, welcome to old age. Making generalisations about age cohorts is risky, but the data really do show that over-55s are drinking more, taking more drugs and having more casual sex, as young people do much less. Although this might seem a last hedonistic hurrah, our report suggests an unhappy reason for oldies misbehaving.
